title: Databricks SDK HTTP requests (tracking, evaluation judges): non-streaming responses must have their body read so the connection returns to the pool
answers: Notebook or long-running MLflow evaluation hangs silently after many Databricks calls, e.g. a judge run stalls on the 21st iteration
Why does a Databricks-backed MLflow REST request leave the connection checked out, and where is the response body consumed?
How do I make a new streaming option (stream=True) on a Databricks SDK request keep its unread response?
Where is the Databricks SDK response from http_request handled before being returned to the caller?
body:
Path: mlflow/utils/rest_utils.py:http_request handles every MLflow REST call routed through the Databricks SDK (`use_databricks_sdk=True`, via `get_workspace_client().api_client.do(..., raw=True)`), including tracking, model registry, and evaluation/judge requests, and returns the underlying `requests`-style response.
Rule: `api_client.do(raw=True)` streams, so the pooled connection stays checked out until the body is read. In the SDK branch of `http_request`, read `response.content` unless the caller passed `stream=True`; streaming callers get the unconsumed response back unchanged. Keep this check next to the `raw_response["contents"]._response` return so any new SDK-backed path inherits it.
Symptom: Long-lived Databricks sessions slowly exhausted the HTTP connection pool, and MLflow calls (e.g. `mlflow.genai.evaluate` with LLM judges) hung silently after roughly 20 successful requests instead of erroring.
Constraints: Applies only to the Databricks SDK branch of http_request. Does not apply to plain `requests` sessions or to callers that explicitly stream; do not consume the body for `stream=True`, since that would defeat streaming.
applies: Any code in mlflow/utils/rest_utils.py that sends requests through the Databricks SDK api_client with raw=True, for any MLflow feature that talks to a Databricks workspace.
says: Notebook evaluation with LLM judges silently hangs after about 20 Databricks calls

search: Databricks SDK HTTP path in http_request: raw streamed responses keep the pooled connection checked out until the body is read, so read the content unless the caller passed stream true. Leaving bodies unread exhausts the connection pool and hangs calls silently after about 20 requests. Applies only to the SDK branch; do not consume bodies for streaming callers or plain requests sessions.
